messages:
anya: Heads-up: noticed a p99 spike on /generate in us-west during the 09:12 traffic burst. Baseline ~3200ms -> sustained ~12s for ~6 minutes. Not a full outage but very noisy for customers.

santiago: seeing same in traces. span-level traces show repeated kernel switches and KV cache misses mid-request. Looks like the runtime started 'probing' an alternate kernel path when queue depth hit ~40.

santiago: snippet from node logs:```
[09:12:07.432] kernel_probe: seq_len_dist=short->long (probing)
[09:12:07.435] kernel_select: chosen=fallback_fastmul_q4_0
[09:12:07.436] kv_cache: hit=false prefetch=false
[09:12:07.439] request_latency_ms=11867
```

jun: pinging autoscaler metrics — there was a burst-adaptive scale-up but cooldown was still 45s from previous shrink. Warm pool had only 2 kept instances; scale request queued while kernels churned.

infra-bot: deploy-bot reports: no deploys at 09:10-09:15. Canary flags unchanged.

maria: quick profiler heatmap (aggregate 09:10-09:18):
- kernel-switch events: +420% vs baseline
- kv-miss-rate: from 6% -> 24% during peak
- batching: avg batch size dropped 30% (more single-shot fallbacks)

anya: interesting — so probe->fallback caused KV prefetch path to be bypassed, causing a cascade of cold KV lookups and longer runtimes, which delayed autoscale handoff and promoted more probes. Looks like a positive feedback loop.

santiago: root cause hypothesis: a recent heuristic tweak to kernel probing (PR #3421) added aggressive probing for savings on short sequences, but under bursty mix the estimator misclassified sequence distribution mid-stream and forced kernel swaps.

jun: immediate mitigations I can push: rollback PR #3421 on the canary pool, bump warm_pool.min from 2 -> 6, and reduce scale-down cooldown from 45s -> 15s for the next 30m window. Want to do these in that order? @santiago @anya

santiago: +1 to rollback first. I'll prepare a small revert and mark kernel_probe_DISABLED flag for canary. Also adding a temporary guard: don't probe if queue_depth > 25.

anya: agree. Jun — do warm-pool bump after rollback. Keep an eye on KV hit-rate. Also notify support about higher p99 for affected customers.

opsbot: alert created: INC-2020 - us-west /generate p99 spike 09:12-09:18. Page owners: eng-runtime oncall.

jun: rolling back PR now to canary (15s). will follow with warm_pool change.

infra-bot: rollout status: canary revert completed at 09:13:12; kernel_probe flag toggled for 3 nodes.

maria: KV hit-rate climbed back toward baseline within ~90s after revert. p99 dropped to ~3.4s within 2min and back to ~3.1s by 09:16. Batch sizes recovered slowly.

anya: nice work. Postmortem action items: 1) revert permanent until we add queue_depth guard and sequence-length smoothing, 2) add e2e test for kernel-probing under bursty seq distribution, 3) make autoscaler warm-pool min adaptive to burst percentiles, 4) add metric for kernel-switch churn to alert earlier. I'll start a short follow-up doc.

santiago: capturing notes and filing ticket PERF-889 with logs + profiler tarball.

jun: follow-ups done: warm_pool.min bumped (ephemeral window), scale-down cooldown shortened for region. Monitoring dashboard annotated.

anya: closing thread for now — reopen if p99 resurges. :thumbsup:
